# Plan: SPE round r01 for the triage agent

This is round r01. The repo has no `spe/` folder yet, so step 0 creates it. There is no earlier round. The control regrade gate does not apply this round, and the plan logs that as skipped. I commit locally after each step. I do not push.

## 1. Specify

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns exactly one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, outage. | User: "triage tickets" | Code check: the value is in the enum |
| R2 | The agent assigns exactly one priority from P1, P2, P3, P4. | User: "triage tickets" | Code check: the value is in the enum |
| R3 | The agent drafts a first reply for each ticket. | Project brief | Code check: reply is present and 40 to 250 words |
| R4 | Output is one JSON object with fields `category`, `priority`, `reply`, `rationale`. | Decision D5 | Code check: JSON schema validation |
| R5 | The category matches the support lead's label. | User: "correctly" | Code check: exact match to the reference label |
| R6 | The priority matches the support lead's label. Exact match and within-one match are both reported. Within-one is the headline. | User: "correctly", Decision D1 | Code check: exact match and absolute difference of at most 1 |
| R7 | The agent does not miss P1 tickets. | Decision D1 | Code check: recall on reference P1 tickets |
| R8 | The reply addresses the customer's issue, invents no facts, promises no refunds, credits, or fix dates, and asks for missing details when needed. | Decision D4 | Judge: rubric with 4 pass/fail items. All 4 must pass. |
| R9 | Mean cost per ticket stays at or below $0.010. | User: "cheaply", Decision D2 | Code check: token counts times the pinned price |
| R10 | The agent sees only the ticket text. It never sees reference labels, graders, or predictions. | Evaluative rule | Transcript scan. A trial that peeked is voided. |

### Open decisions and logged defaults (go to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default I chose | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What "correctly" means | Category exact match. Priority within one as the headline, with exact match also reported. P1 recall reported on its own. | User |
| D2 | What "cheaply" means | Mean cost per ticket at or below $0.010 | User |
| D3 | Priority definitions | P1 means service down or data loss for many customers. P2 means a core feature is broken for one customer or a group. P3 means a minor bug or a blocked how-to. P4 means a question or request with no impact. | Support lead |
| D4 | What a good reply is | The 4-item rubric in R8 | User |
| D5 | Where the 40 tickets live | `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` holds id, subject, and body. `spe/evals/data/labels.jsonl` holds id, category, and priority. Trials cannot read the labels file. | User |
| D6 | Which models the product may use | Configs use a pinned Sonnet-tier model and a pinned Haiku-tier model. I confirm exact model IDs and prices against current Anthropic docs before the dry run. | User |
| D7 | Where few-shot examples come from | I write 5 synthetic tickets from the D3 definitions. None comes from the 40 eval tickets. | User |
| D8 | Who judges replies | A pinned Opus-tier model that is separate from every config under test | User |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each config changes one thing from C1.

| Config | Model | Prompt | Changed from C1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Sonnet tier (pinned) | Definitions only, zero-shot | Reference |
| C2 | Sonnet tier (pinned) | Definitions plus 5 synthetic examples | Prompt adds examples |
| C3 | Haiku tier (pinned) | Definitions only, zero-shot | Model only |

### Numeric prediction

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. Each cell is the mean over 40 tickets and 3 repeats.

| Metric | C1 | C2 | C3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid rate | 0.99 ± 0.02 | 0.99 ± 0.02 | 0.97 ± 0.03 | `check_schema` | Structured JSON output rarely fails on these models. The smaller model fails slightly more. |
| Category accuracy | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.07 | 0.78 ± 0.08 | `check_category_exact` | Billing and account overlap, and bug and outage overlap. Examples help with those edges. |
| Priority exact | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.65 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.10 | `check_priority_exact` | One person set the reference priorities, and priority judgments vary between people. |
| Priority within one | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.93 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | `check_priority_within_one` | Most priority misses are off by one level. |
| P1 recall | 0.80 ± 0.15 | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.70 ± 0.15 | `check_p1_recall` | Outage wording is clear. The band is wide because the set likely holds only about 5 P1 tickets. |
| Reply pass rate | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.87 ± 0.08 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | `judge_reply_rubric` | The most likely failure is a reply that promises a fix date or a credit. |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | 0.012 ± 0.004 | 0.016 ± 0.005 | 0.004 ± 0.002 | `check_cost` | I assume about 2,000 input and 400 output tokens per ticket. C2 adds about 1,200 input tokens. |

`same_as_last_round` is not applicable in r01.

The naive guess for comparison assigns the most common category and P3 to every ticket. The harness computes its scores from the label distribution and logs them next to the results.

I expect C1 and C2 to miss the R9 cost bar and C3 to meet it. I also expect C3 to cost about 7 points of category accuracy. Round r02 then has a real trade-off for you to decide.

## 3. Evaluate

### Steps after approval

Each step ends with a local commit. Commit messages name no author tool.

0. **Scaffold.** Create the `spe/` tree and `spe/README.md`. Save your prompt and planning answers verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`. Write `spe/spec/spec.md` and `spe/spec/disagreements.md` from the tables above. Commit `spe(r01): scaffold and spec`.
1. **Save the prediction.** Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds the round, the date 2026-10-21, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round: n/a`. Commit `spe(r01): plan and prediction`.
2. **Build the agent.** Write the triage prompt, the output schema, and a runner that takes one ticket and one config. Write the 5 synthetic examples for C2. Commit `triage: agent prompt, schema, runner`.
3. **Build the graders and harness.** Write code checks first, then the judge rubric. Put the labels in a path the trial sandbox cannot read. Write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` with one `ROUND = "r01"` constant. Commit `spe(r01): graders and harness`.
4. **Run the gates in order.** Each gate must pass before the next one runs.
   - Grader selftest. The oracle answer, which is the reference labels plus a clean reply, must score 40/40. An empty answer and a shifted wrong-label answer must fail.
   - Control regrade. This gate is skipped in r01 because no earlier round exists. The harness logs the skip.
   - Dry run on 3 cells: C1, C2, and C3, with 1 ticket each. I check the schema, the cost logging, and the transcript scan.
   - Commit `spe(r01): gates passed`.
5. **Launch the Workflow.** The Workflow returns at launch. I close out when its completion notice arrives.

### Workflow arguments

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | `"r01"` |
| `configs` | `["C1", "C2", "C3"]` |
| `tickets` | `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` (40 tickets) |
| `repeats` | 3 per ticket per config, for 360 trials |
| `extra_repeats_on_split` | Up to 2 more repeats when a cell's repeats differ by more than 0.10 on any accuracy metric |
| `judge` | Pinned Opus-tier model, replies only |
| `spend_cap_usd` | 25. A trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged. |
| `peek_scan` | Void any trial whose transcript touches `labels.jsonl`, `graders/`, or `predictions/` |
| `final_steps` | Failure analysis, then a completeness critic |

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Agent trials (360) | about $4 |
| Judge calls (360) | about $11 |
| Workflow orchestration overhead | not estimated yet. The run logs it. |
| Total expected | about $15, under the $25 cap |

### Halt conditions

The run halts and reports to you if it hits the spend cap, finds a leaked label, finds a broken grader, or reaches a decision only you can make.

### Close-out (after the completion notice)

- Write `spe/prediction-log.md` with predicted and measured values, a verdict per cell, and "Which Why broke". It also says plainly whether the naive guess beat any prediction.
- Write `spe/failures.md` with F-numbered failure types.
- Add a "Proposed for round r02" table to the spec and save `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Update `spe/README.md`, commit `spe(r01): learn`, and tag `spe-r01` locally. Nothing is pushed.
critiques: The Requirements table turns the user's prompt into R1 to R10. Each row cites a source such as User: "correctly" or User: "cheaply", and each row has a Test column, for example "Code check: exact match to the reference label". Open terms are logged as defaults D1 to D8.

The Numeric prediction table gives every config a number with a band on every metric. For example, Category accuracy is 0.85 ± 0.07 for C1, 0.88 ± 0.07 for C2, and 0.78 ± 0.08 for C3. Cost per ticket is given in USD for each config.

Each metric row has a Why column. Examples are "Billing and account overlap, and bug and outage overlap" and the token assumption behind the cost numbers. The reason is given per metric row and not per cell, but it covers all three configs and explains the gaps between them.

Step 1 copies the plan to spe/plans/r01.md and writes spe/predictions/r01.yaml with a do-not-edit header. It then commits "spe(r01): plan and prediction". This happens before the build, the gates, and the Workflow launch in steps 2 to 5.

Step 4 runs gates in order. A grader selftest must score the oracle at 40/40 and must fail the empty and shifted answers. A 3-cell dry run follows. Step 5 then launches the Workflow with the listed arguments.
The prediction table has a Grader check column. It ties each metric to a named check, such as check_schema, check_priority_within_one, check_p1_recall, judge_reply_rubric, and check_cost.

The Close-out writes spe/prediction-log.md with predicted and measured values, a verdict per cell, and "Which Why broke". It also checks the result against the naive guess. It seeds round r02 with a "Proposed for round r02" table and spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml.
